title: Frobenius from adapted fields to global limits
promptMarkdown: Prove the local Frobenius theorem for a smooth constant-rank distribution using the graph-form frame $X_i$ in the lesson. Explain why involutivity makes those fields commute and how their flows form coordinates. Complete your account with the irrational-slope torus example: establish injectivity and density of a leaf, and explain why neither a global embedded leaf nor a Hausdorff leaf space follows from the local theorem. Relate this limitation to what holonomy and Reeb stability add.
hintLadder: Make the horizontal projection invertible before choosing the frame.
Zero bracket makes local flows commute.
Distinguish the topology on the line parameter from the topology of its image.
